# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this repo is

Not a software project — it's the content/automation pipeline for an Instagram
recruitment account ("フリーランス美容師の働き方&求人", `@freelance_biyoshi_kyujin`)
for a hair salon (piece201, Nakameguro). There is no build/lint/test suite; the
"product" is Instagram carousel posts generated by Python scripts and published
via Metricool.

Full history/decisions/all captions: `docs/handover.md`. Step-by-step how-to for
the whole pipeline: `docs/guide.md`. Read `docs/guide.md` before doing pipeline
work if this is your first turn in this repo — it has the exact commands.

## Hard rules — do not skip these

1. **Never generate images before the user approves the slide structure + full
   caption text.** Always draft and present both first, wait for explicit OK,
   only then call `build_postN()`.
2. **Never call the Metricool `createScheduledPost` tool without an explicit
   instruction to publish/schedule** (e.g. "投稿して"). Drafting and generating
   images is not permission to post.
3. **Schedule at least 20 minutes ahead of the current time.** Shorter buffers
   cause `createScheduledPost` to fail with "Publication date cannot be in the
   past" — cloud sessions can have long, unpredictable real-time gaps between
   turns (seen gaps of 10+ hours between consecutive messages), so always
   re-run `date` to get the actual current time immediately before computing
   publish times — never reuse a time computed earlier in the conversation.
4. **`getScheduledPosts`'s `status`/`detailedStatus` field for Instagram posts
   is not reliable — it has shown `"ERROR"` (`"We restrict certain activity to
   protect our community..."`) for posts that had, in fact, already published
   successfully.** (Discovered 2026-09-23: 13–15本目 all showed `ERROR` on
   2026-09-17/18, which was read as a real Instagram auto-restriction and
   drove a whole cadence-policy change — daily posting → 3-day spacing,
   `autoPublish: false`. Checking the Instagram Posts analytics connector
   (`getAnalyticsDataByMetrics` with `IGPO01/02/03/06` on the `posts`
   connector for `instagram`) later showed 11–16本目 *all* actually
   auto-published on schedule, one per day, 9/13–9/18. The daily cadence was
   never the problem; there is no confirmed bot-pattern restriction on this
   account.** Before treating a `getScheduledPosts` error as real, cross-check
   with the analytics connector (it reflects Instagram's own post history,
   not Metricool's internal scheduling state) or ask the user to check the
   Instagram app directly — don't diagnose or change policy off
   `getScheduledPosts` status alone. Note: fetching instagram.com directly
   (WebFetch) is blocked by network egress policy in this environment — the
   analytics connector is the only way to check Instagram's actual state
   from here. To pull the real post history: `getAnalyticsAvailableMetrics`
   (`network: instagram`, `connector: posts`) to see fields, then
   `getAnalyticsDataByMetrics` with `["IGPO01","IGPO02","IGPO03","IGPO06"]`
   (date / datetime / caption / post URL) over the date range in question.
   Full incident writeup: `docs/handover.md` section 11, "重大インシデント記録".
5. **Before calling `updateScheduledPost` on any post, re-check that exact
   post's current status first (ideally via the analytics connector, not
   just `getScheduledPosts` — see #4) — never reuse an older status
   snapshot, especially when batch-fixing several posts at once.**
   (2026-09-18: a batch reschedule of 13–16本目 reused a stale `ERROR`
   snapshot for posts whose *original* `autoPublish: true` attempts had,
   unknown to us, already succeeded and gone live on Instagram.
   `updateScheduledPost` overwrites the same uuid's date/content with no
   awareness of whether it already published, so this left phantom
   future-dated duplicates for 15/16本目 — neutralized with `draft: true`
   once caught. No actual double-post resulted this time, confirmed via the
   Instagram grid, but don't count on that.)
6. **Cadence: post as soon as content is ready, capped at 1/day, `autoPublish:
   true`.** (Reverted 2026-09-23: the "space 3 days, `autoPublish: false`"
   policy from #4/#5's incident was itself based on the false ERROR
   diagnosis — the account handled daily `autoPublish: true` posting fine
   for 11–16本目. The user explicitly asked to revert to daily cadence.) Use
   `getScheduledPosts` to find the next open day and `getBestTimeToPostByNetwork`
   for that day's best hour; schedule ≥20 min ahead per #3.
   **⚠️ SUPERSEDED as of 2026-09-23 — see the "Story catch-up initiative"
   below: new feed carousel posts are paused for now in favor of a daily
   Story series. Resume this cadence rule once the user says the catch-up
   is done / gives the go-ahead to post new feed content again.**

## Media hosting (for Metricool's `media` field)

**Use the GitHub raw URL of the already-committed image — do not use Google
Drive.** `createScheduledPost`'s `media` field needs a public URL; since every
generated image is committed and pushed to this repo anyway (hard rule #10),
and the repo is public, `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/<repo>/<branch>/<path>`
is a public URL with zero extra steps:

```
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masu1234567masu/biyoshi_kyujin/claude/automation-planning-verification-lcupt0/assets/posts/<dir>/<file>.jpg
```

Order of operations: generate → **commit & push first** → then schedule with
the raw URL (Metricool fetches it live, so the push must land before the
`createScheduledPost` call) → no cleanup step needed (nothing to delete,
unlike Drive).

**⚠️ Retired 2026-10-11 — do not use `scripts/drive_upload.py` /
`scripts/oauth_step1_get_auth_url.py` / `scripts/oauth_step2_exchange_code.py`
for new posts.** They're left in the repo for reference only. Reason: this
runs in an ephemeral cloud container that's wiped on every new session, and
`secrets/` is (correctly) gitignored — so every session needed a fresh,
human-in-the-loop OAuth re-consent before any image could be scheduled. That
friction (and the 2026-10-11 incident where a container reset also lost the
one-time `oauth_client_secret.json` itself, blocking re-auth entirely until
the user re-supplied it) is exactly what the GitHub-raw-URL approach
eliminates — no credentials, no re-auth, ever.

## Architecture

Pipeline: **draft/approve → generate images (Pillow) → commit & push to get a
public GitHub raw URL → `createScheduledPost` via the Metricool MCP tool →
update handover.md → commit/push.**

`scripts/generate_all_slides.py` is one file containing every post's image
recipe. Each post is a `build_postN()` function (N = 5, 7–16 so far) that
calls shared layout primitives:
- `draw_cover_slide()` — title slide
- `draw_title_body_slide()` — heading + body, the workhorse for numbered
  point slides (①②③...)
- `draw_comparison_row_slide()` — "A vs B" comparison table
- `draw_closing_slide()` — combined summary + DM-CTA slide (always the last
  slide; never split summary and CTA into two slides)
- `fit_font()` — auto-shrinks font size so text never overflows the 1080px
  canvas; all the `draw_*` functions already call it, so new text doesn't
  need special handling for long strings

To add a new post: copy the most recent `build_postN()`, adjust text, add it
to the `if __name__ == "__main__"` block at the bottom, generate, then eyeball
the rendered slides (Read tool) before uploading — especially cover slides
and any comparison tables, where overflow bugs have happened before.

`config/drive_config.json` holds the Metricool `brandId` (`6852890`) and
timezone (`Asia/Tokyo`) — read from there rather than hardcoding if it might
change. (It also still has Drive-related fields from the retired upload
path; ignore those — see "Media hosting" above.)

## Content/domain knowledge worth knowing upfront

- Three distinct hairdresser employment terms used precisely throughout —
  don't conflate them: **面貸し/フリーランス** (booth rental, full commission
  60–70%, no salon-provided new clients, free schedule — this is piece201's
  actual arrangement), **業務委託** (commission ~40–50%, salon brings new
  clients, some time constraints), **雇用** (salaried + 10–20% commission,
  most constrained).
- Captions cap at 5 hashtags (Instagram display limit).
- Post body copy stays salon-neutral; piece201 gets mentioned only in the
  closing slide/caption CTA, never mid-post (this account is meant to grow
  into a multi-salon media property later).
- Emoji render as "✕" if drawn into the Pillow images (the CJK fonts have no
  emoji glyphs) — emoji only belong in caption text, never in
  `draw_*_slide()` calls.
